findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, and no ACL is set (defaults to private but unconfirmed), meaning report data is stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely financial/sensitive) without any server_side_encryption_configuration, meaning data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest despite having versioning and logging enabled.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbook content (potentially containing sensitive operational details or credentials) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; this appears to be a typo for 'log-delivery-write' and will likely cause apply-time failure or unintended access behavior, undermining the intended access control for this sensitive audit trail bucket.

This object is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configured, meaning the vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor/PII data) is stored unencrypted at rest.
